conflicts.fact: What the cumulative model started in Lesson 1 contains, and what it is called
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: students build a 'Data Story Map' showing raw list, frequency table and '???'. Lesson 2: students revise a 'predictive model' from Lesson 1, a sketch of how to find the 'one best number'. Lesson 3: the 'Data Story Model' got the raw data list in Lesson 1 and the frequency table in Lesson 2, although Lesson 1 already built the frequency table.

conflicts.fact: Name and origin of the cumulative model
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1, 3, 7, 8 and 9 call it the 'Data Story Map' or 'Data Story Model' (started in Lesson 1). Lesson 4 has 'My Statistical Toolkit', and Lesson 5 calls the 'Statistical Toolkit' diagram a model 'built since Lesson 3'.
Lesson 7 says the mode was covered in 'Lessons 3–6'. Mode was taught only in Lesson 4, Lesson 3 covered the mean, and Lessons 5 and 6 covered the median and line graphs.

conflicts.fact: Wording of the driving question on the DQB
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says the DQB shows the original question 'Which single number best represents all our farmers — and how do we even begin to make sense of all this data?'. Lessons 2, 3, 4, 7 and 9 give the driving question as 'How can we collect, organize, and represent data about our community to help Kenyan decision-makers take effective action?'.

conflicts.fact: Content of the bar graph in the dossier
conflicts.versions: The Lesson 9 overview says a bar graph of maize yields 'per county over two seasons'. The Observe phase and Observed summary say yields by Nakuru sub-county across two seasons. Lesson 7 bar graphs compare five Rift Valley counties by harvest frequency.
